lines: - `admin.auth.cookie.name` (default `jwtToken`) — name of the non-httpOnly access-token cookie used for session logins (when `rememberMe` is false) and EE SSO handoff. Rename to avoid collisions with another app on a shared parent domain that sets a `jwtToken` cookie. Requires an admin rebuild after change (value is inlined into the admin bundle at build time).

- `admin.auth.cookie.domain` (or `admin.auth.domain`) — applied to `strapi_admin_refresh` and to the non-httpOnly access-token cookie written by the admin client (and EE SSO). Defaults to a host-only cookie when unset. Requires an admin rebuild after change (value is inlined into the admin bundle at build time). Set a parent domain to share the admin session across subdomains; leave unset to keep each host isolated.

-  - `admin.auth.cookie.path` (default `/admin`) — applied to `strapi_admin_refresh` and to the non-httpOnly access-token cookie written by the admin client (and EE SSO). Requires an admin rebuild after change (value is inlined into the admin bundle at build time). Use a distinct path per instance when hosting multiple Strapis under the same parent domain.

When unset, the two cookies get different paths, both behind any `server.url` subpath: the access-token cookie uses the path the admin panel is served from (`admin.url`, so `/admin` by default), because only the panel reads it through `document.cookie`; `strapi_admin_refresh` uses the admin API path `/admin`, because only `POST /admin/access-token` and the other `/admin/*` auth routes read it, and those do not move with `admin.url`. A configured path that does not cover the admin API (for example `/dashboard`) is ignored for `strapi_admin_refresh`, with a warning, since the browser would never send the cookie to `/admin/access-token`.
